title: Water and ice
hookLine: the visualizations continue: water, ice, crystal ground

lines: A BOWL OF WATER ON A WINTER NIGHT.
cards: A bowl of water left out on a winter night. By morning it has gone hard and clear, and when you hold it up, the light comes straight through. Nothing was added.
Nothing was taken away. The water simply went still, all the way down. That small, ordinary change is the next step in the meditations of the sutra Pure Land Buddhists call the Contemplation Sutra.
After the sun, the queen is shown water, and the water does not stay water for long. Today: water and ice.

teach.h: WATER, THEN ICE, THEN A JEWEL GROUND.
teach.b: First, the steps. After the setting sun, the sutra describes a second contemplation. Look at water, and see it clear and pure, so clear the mind does not scatter.
Then see the water as ice, shining and transparent. Then let the ice become a ground of jewel, clear inside and out, with light streaming up from beneath it.
That ground, the sutra says, is the ground of the land of bliss. Second, why water comes next. A sunset is far away; you can only look at it.
Water is something anyone has held in a cupped hand, felt cold, poured out. The picture moves closer. And the water isn't swapped for something else.
It changes state, water to ice, ice to jewel, the same clearness carried through each change. Third, the stillness.

teach.h: STILL WATER LETS THE LIGHT THROUGH.
teach.b: Water only shows a clear picture when it stops moving, and ice is water that has stopped completely.

teach.h: SOME PICTURE IT; SOME CALL THE NAME.
teach.b: Some readers hear the mind in this: stirred, it clouds; settled, the light gets through. The sutra itself doesn't spell that out. It simply asks for the picture, held steadily, eyes open or closed.
Fourth, how it lives today. Some Pure Land practitioners work through these pictures in order, slowly, one at a time.
For others, the name of Amitabha is the center, and the pictures stay in the sutra as a doorway they know is there.
Either way, the instruction is the same: one clear picture, held steady.

how: Some Pure Land practitioners work through the Contemplation Sutra's visualizations in order, from the setting sun to water, ice and the jewel ground; others center their practice on calling Amitabha's name and know the visualizations through reading.

o: the sutra's second picture: water turning to clear ice
a cold-water ritual meant to purify the body first
a ritual washing done before Pure Land chanting

games.q: the water contemplation: tap the pairs.

s: the water contemplation stays with water the whole time
it moves: water, then shining ice, then a ground of jewel, clear inside and out.
in the sutra, the jewel ground is the ground of the land of bliss
the pictures climb from ordinary water to the ground of the Pure Land itself.
every Pure Land practitioner works through the visualizations
some do, in order; for others the name of Amitabha is the center.

games.q: you're holding the picture of clear water, and it starts to ripple and fade. what does the practice ask?
o: let it settle and hold it steadily again.
games.why: the sutra asks for the picture held steadily. like water, the mind can settle again, and then the light comes through.

practice: Bring to mind water you've actually seen, a glass, a basin, a lake on a calm morning, and let it go still, clear enough to see the bottom. If the picture ripples or fades, let it settle again, the way water does on its own.
If it comes easily, let the water turn to clear ice, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: Water and ice. The second contemplation of the Contemplation Sutra: clear water becomes shining ice, and the ice becomes the jewel ground of the land of bliss. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: clear as water. The same clearness, from water to ice to jewel. Until tomorrow.
